column3: The Hebrew says David left “there” and escaped, without explicitly repeating Gath; BSB names Gath and says he took refuge.
The Hebrew repeats “every man” for each group and describes the discontented as “bitter of soul”; BSB condenses the three groups.
The request literally asks that the parents go out with them; BSB says “stay with you”.
David actively led them before the king; BSB has “left them in the care of” the king.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul twice and Gibeah once; BSB substitutes a time expression for the second Saul and repeats Gibeah.
The Hebrew repeats “all of you” and joins commanders of thousands and hundreds with “and”; BSB has “or”.
Informing is twice described as uncovering an ear; BSB replaces both bodily images with telling or revealing.
The Hebrew states he was standing with Saul’s servants; BSB says he had stationed himself there.
The first inquirer is unnamed as “he”; BSB supplies Ahimelech’s name.
“Messengers” is supplied to complete the Hebrew “the king sent to summon”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes David’s relation to the bodyguard without explicitly calling him its captain; BSB supplies that title.
The Hebrew asks about “today”, not “that day”, and says “small or great”; BSB has “in part or in whole”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The guards are called runners; informing is uncovering the ear, and siding with David is having their hand with him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The sword is twice described as having a mouth; BSB condenses this to one “put to the sword”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to each “soul” of the household; BSB has “the lives of everyone”.
The Hebrew first names the one seeking my soul and then says he seeks yours; BSB reverses the order of the two lives.
